1 Safety instructions
General safety instructions
This appliance can be used by children aged from 8 years and above and persons with reduced physical, sensory or mental 
capabilities or lack of experience and knowledge if they have been given supervision or instruction concerning use of the 
appliance in a safe way and understand the hazards involved. Children shall not play with the appliance. Children must not carry 
out any unsupervised cleaning or maintenance operations.
Before any work, read the documents provided with the appliance carefully. These documents are also available on our website. 
See the back cover.
Keep these documents close to the place where the appliance is installed.
Only qualified professionals are authorised to carry out installation, commissioning, maintenance, repair or removal work on the 
appliance. They must follow the prevailing local and national regulations.
Do not make any modifications to the appliance without the written consent of the manufacturer. To benefit from warranty cover, 
no modifications should be made to the appliance.
Installation location
The indoor unit must be installed in a frost-free room.
Allow sufficient space around the appliance to ensure adequate accessibility to the appliance to facilitate maintenance. See 
"Installation" chapter.
Instructions for using glycol water
Ensure that all the installation components are compatible with the use of glycol water.
Only use high-quality food-grade glycol water solutions based on monopropylene glycol (MPG).
Use a monopropylene glycol solution concentration which is compatible with the appliance. See the chapter on Precautions to 
take when filling with glycol water.
Electrical connections
Only a qualified installer or a qualified technician is authorised to work on the appliance's electrical system, as an incorrectly 
performed intervention may cause electrical shocks and/or electrical leakage.
Install the appliance in accordance with national rules on electrical installation.
In order to avoid the danger of an unexpected thermal circuit breaker reset, this appliance must not be powered through an 
external switch, such as a timer, or be connected to a circuit which is regularly switched on and off by the electricity provider.
Before any wiring work on the electrical circuit, switch off the power supply, check that no voltage is present and secure the 
circuit breaker with a circuit breaker lockout.
Use wiring that meets the specifications in the installation manual and local regulations and laws. Use of wiring which does not 
meet the specifications may give rise to electric shocks, electrical leakage, smoke and/or a fire.
This appliance must be connected to the protective earthing in accordance with prevailing installation standards. Earth the 
appliance before making any electrical connections. Incomplete grounding can cause a malfunction or electric shock.
To avoid electric shock, check that the length of the conductors between the cable clamp and the terminal blocks is such that 
the active conductors are put under tension before the earth conductor.
Install a circuit breaker that meets the specifications in the installation manual and local regulations and laws.
If a power supply cable comes with the appliance and it turns out to be damaged, it must be replaced by the manufacturer, its 
after-sales service or persons with similar qualifications in order to avoid danger.
Separate the extra-low voltage cables from the 230/400 V power supply cables.
See the Electrical connections chapter for the following operations:
Choosing the type and calibre of the protective equipment
Connection to the electrical network
Wiring the appliance
Maintenance and repair work
Remove the casing only to perform maintenance and repair work. Put the casing back in place after maintenance and repair 
work.
Repair and maintenance of electrical components must include initial safety checks and component inspection procedures. In 
the event of a fault that could compromise safety, no power supply may be connected to the circuit until said fault has been 
dealt with satisfactorily. If the fault cannot be corrected immediately but it is necessary to continue operation, an appropriate 
temporary solution must be adopted. This shall be reported to the owner of the equipment to ensure all parties are duly 
informed.
Initial safety checks shall include:

pages.7:
Discharging of the capacitors: this shall be done in a safe manner to avoid any possibility of sparking
Ensuring no live electrical components and wiring are exposed while charging, recovering or draining the system
Ensuring the continuity of the earth bonding.
Before any work, switch off the power supply for all the components of your installation.
Use only original spare parts.
Guidelines for the user
If you do not need to heat your home for a long period, deactivate the heating mode. Do not switch off the heat pump in order to 
guarantee the frost protection of the installation.
If you do need to switch off the heat pump and if there is a risk that the temperature inside and/or outside the building will fall 
below zero:
Installation filled with mains water: drain the water pipes of the installation (heat pump, underfloor heating, etc.) to prevent the 
system from freezing
Installation filled with glycol water: the installation is protected against freezing
Keep the appliance accessible at all times to allow work to be performed.
Never remove or cover the labels and data plates affixed to appliances. These must be legible throughout the entire lifetime of 
the appliance.
Manufacturer's liabilities
Our products are manufactured in compliance with the requirements of the various applicable directives. They are therefore 
delivered with the marking and any documents necessary. In the interests of the quality of our products, we strive constantly 
to improve them. We therefore reserve the right to modify the specifications given in this document.
Our liability as manufacturer may not be invoked in the following cases:
Failure to abide by the instructions on installing, commissioning and maintaining the appliance
Failure to abide by the instructions on using the appliance
Faulty or insufficient maintenance of the appliance
Responsibilities of the installer
The installer is responsible for the installation and initial commissioning of the appliance. The installer must observe the 
following instructions:
Read and follow the instructions given in the manuals provided with the appliance
Install the appliance in compliance with prevailing legislation and standards
Carry out initial commissioning and any checks necessary
Explain the installation to the user
If maintenance is necessary, warn the user of the obligation to check the appliance and keep it in good working order
Hand over all manuals to the user
Responsibilities of the user
To guarantee optimum operation of the system, you must abide by the following instructions:
Read and follow the instructions given in the manuals provided with the appliance
Call on a qualified professional to carry out installation and initial commissioning
Get your installer to explain your installation to you
Have the required inspections and maintenance carried out by a qualified installer
Keep the instruction manuals in good condition close to the appliance

6 Installation
6.1 Installation regulations
Caution
The appliance must be installed by a qualified professional in 
accordance with applicable local and national regulations.
6.2 Positioning the indoor unit
6.2.1 Choosing the location of the indoor unit
The location of the indoor unit must guarantee safety, be accessible for 
maintenance, allow the front panel to be removed and the cover on the 
user interface to be flipped up.
1. Take account of the dimensions shown opposite when choosing the 
location of the indoor unit.
2. Choose a location that complies with the following specifications:
not exposed to water or dust
close to a wall socket with protective earthing
allow sufficient space for work on the indoor unit
6.2.2 Affixing the indoor unit
Once the location has been chosen for the unit, affix the indoor unit using 
the side tabs.
1. Mark the positions of the 4 holes.
2. Drill the Ø 6 mm holes.
3. Insert the Ø 6 mm wall plugs.
4. Secure the indoor unit using Ø 3.5 mm screws.
6.3 Respect the maximum pipe length between the outdoor unit and the heating zone
To ensure correct operation of the heat pump:
1. Identify the output of the outdoor unit using the data plate.
2. Respect the maximum pipe length between the outdoor unit and the 
heating zone. 
The equivalent flue length to a 90° bend is 1 metre.
3. The maximum pipe length between the diverter valve and the 
domestic hot water cylinder must not exceed 10 metres. 
The equivalent flue length to a 90° bend is 1 metre.
4. Respect the internal diameter of the pipes.

6.4 Hydraulic connections
6.4.1 Special precautions for the connection of the heating circuit
Caution
The hydraulic installation must be capable of handling a minimum 
flow rate at all times:
If radiators are connected directly to the heating circuit, install a 
pressure actuated bypass valve between the outdoor unit and 
the heating circuit,
Otherwise, leave the heating circuit without a thermostatic valve 
and/or without a solenoid valve.
When making the connection, always comply with the applicable local 
standards and directives.
Ensure that the EPDM sealing elements do not come into contact with 
substances containing mineral oil. Products containing mineral oil will 
cause permanent serious damage to the material, causing it to lose its 
impermeability.
If components made from composite materials are used (for example, 
polyethylene connection pipes or flexible hose), we recommend 
components with an anti-oxygen barrier.
6.4.2 Minimum volume of water
The volume of water in the installation must be sufficient to avoid short 
cycle operation and to enable optimal defrosting.
Important
The minimum volume of water in circulation must be available at 
any time, even if there is no heating demand or when all the 
valves are closed.
If the volume of water in circulation is not sufficient, it is necessary to 
install a buffer tank with the additional volume.

6.4.5 Outdoor unit frost protection
In normal operation, the outdoor unit and the heating circuit are protected 
from frost.
To protect the outdoor unit during prolonged power outages and outdoor 
temperatures below zero, one of the following solutions must be installed:
Solution using glycol
Addition of glycol to the heating circuit.
Refer to local regulations and system component manuals to check

6.5.10 Scenarios when a backup is necessary
Caution
If no backup is connected, the comfort in heating and domestic hot 
water mode and frost protection of the appliance may not be 
guaranteed, the life of the heat pump may be reduced and safety 
problems may be caused.
A backup is mandatory in the following cases:
The heat pump is not designed to cover 100% of the building's heat 
loss.
The outside air temperature may be outside the heat pump's operating 
limits.
The domestic hot water setpoint is above 53 °C without an immersion 
heater in the domestic hot water cylinder.
Anti-legionella treatment is necessary in a domestic hot water cylinder 
without an immersion heater.
The water temperature in the heating circuit may be below 5 °C:
When commissioning the heat pump.
If the heat pump is not used for a long time.
During a prolonged power cut.

Outdoor unit frost protection, page 24

6.6 Filling and checking the installation
6.6.1 Filling the heating circuit
After flushing the installation and checking that the filters are clean, you 
can fill the heating circuit with water from the distribution network.
1. Check that the automatic bleed valve present on the outdoor unit is 
open (at least 2 turns).
2. Fill the installation until a pressure of 2 bar is reached.
3. Check that there are no leaks.
4. Bleed the installation fully for optimal operation.
6.6.2 Checking the heating circuit
1. Check that the volume of the expansion vessel(s) is sufficient for the 
volume of water in the heating installation. 
2. Check the inflation pressure of the expansion vessel(s).
3. Check that the heating circuit has a sufficient water fill level. If 
necessary, top up the water.
4. Check that the water connections are properly sealed.
5. Check that the heating circuit has been properly vented.
6. Check that the filter is not clogged. Clean it if necessary.
7. Check that the condensates are being correctly drained from the 
outdoor unit.
8. Check that the valves and thermostatic radiator valves are open.
9. Check that all settings and safety devices are working correctly.
10. Check the water quality, after a few operating hours.
11. Vent the heating circuit again.

8.14 Resetting or re-establishing the parameters
8.14.1 Resetting the configuration numbers
If you have replaced the PCB or made an error during setting, you must 
reset the configuration numbers CN1 and CN2. Thanks to these numbers, 
the system recognises the outdoor unit output and the type of backup 
present on the installation.
To reset the configuration numbers:
1. Press the button.
2. Select Installer.
3. Select Advanced menu > Set configuration code > EHC–16.
4. Set the CN1 and CN2 parameters. The values are available on the 
data plate of the indoor unit.
5. Select Confirm to save the settings.
See also
CN1 and CN2 parameters, page 38
8.14.2 Auto-detecting options and accessories
Use this function after replacing a power circuit board on the heat pump in 
order to detect all the devices connected to the L–BUS communication 
bus.
To detect devices connected to the L–BUS communication bus:
1. Press the button.
2. Select Installer.
3. Select Advanced menu > Auto detect.
4. Select Confirm to carry out the auto-detect.
8.14.3 Reverting to the factory settings
To revert to the factory settings for the heat pump:
1. Press the button.
2. Select Installer.
3. Select Advanced menu > Reset to factory settings.
4. Select Confirm to revert to the factory settings.

9.2.2 Running the back-up in heating mode
Start-up conditions for the backup
The backups are authorised to start up normally except in cases of power 
cut-off or limitation linked to bivalency (Bivalent temperature - HP000).
If the heat pump should also be limited, the backups are nevertheless 
authorised to operate to guarantee heating comfort.
In heating mode, the backup is managed by the parameters: Bivalent 
temperature (HP000) and Delay startbackup CH (HP030).
If Delay startbackup CH (HP030) is set to 0, the time delay for start-up of 
the backup is set depending on the outdoor temperature: the lower the 
outdoor temperature, the quicker the backup will be activated.
t Time (minutes)
T Outdoor temperature (°C)
1 Delay min outdoor T (HP047) = 8 minutes
2 Delay max outdoor T (HP048) = 30 minutes
3 Min outdoor T backup (HP049) = -10 °C
4 Max outdoor T backup (HP050) = 15 °C
In this example of a time delay in starting the backup when Delay 
startbackup CH HP030 is set to 0, if the outdoor temperature is 10 °C, the 
backup will start 25 minutes after the heat pump's outdoor unit.
Backup operation if an error occurs on the outdoor unit
If an error occurs on the outdoor unit during a system heat demand, the 
backup boiler or heating element starts up immediately to guarantee 
heating comfort.
Operation when the outdoor temperature falls below the 
operating threshold of the outdoor unit
If the outdoor temperature is below the minimum operating temperature of 
the outdoor unit as defined by the Min outdoor T HP (HP051) parameter, 
the outdoor unit is not authorised to operate.
If the system has a demand pending, the backup boiler or the electric 
heating element (if present) starts up immediately to guarantee heating 
comfort.

9.2.3 Running the back-up in domestic hot water mode
Start-up conditions for the backup
The start-up conditions for the backup for domestic hot water production 
depend on the BL input setting (AP001) and BL2 function (AP100) 
parameters for the blocking inputs BL1 and BL2 respectively.
Operating description
The behaviour of the backup boiler or the electric heating element in 
domestic hot water mode depends on the configuration of the DHW 
management(DP051) parameter.
If DHW management (DP051) is set to HP only the system gives priority to 
the heat pump during domestic hot water production. The backup boiler or 
the electric heating element is used only if the start-up time delay for the 
backup during domestic hot water production Delay StartBackupDHW 
(DP090) has elapsed in domestic hot water mode, unless the hybrid mode 
is activated. In this case, hybrid logic takes over.
If DHW management (DP051) is set to Auto (HP + Boiler) the domestic hot 
water production mode gives priority to comfort by accelerating domestic 
hot water production by simultaneously using the heat pump and the 
backup boiler or the electric heating element. In this mode, there is no 
maximum time for domestic hot water production as the use of the 
backups helps to ensure domestic hot water comfort more quickly.
9.2.4 Operation of the switch between heating and DHW generation
The system does not allow simultaneous central heating and generation of 
domestic hot water, unless the domestic hot water cylinder is equipped 
with an immersion heating element.
The switch logic between domestic hot water mode and heating mode 
operates as follows:

11.3.1 Solar installations with the DrainBack drainage system
DrainBack
The DrainBack is a system with a reservoir that allows the solar collectors 
to drain by gravity whenever the pump stops. The solar collectors are 
thereby protected from freezing and overheating. The control system is 
used to determine the minimum and maximum operating temperatures for 
the pump.

activated and configured alongside the parameters for the type of solar 
installation.

11.3.3 Solar cooling
The solar cooling system transfers the excess heat from the storage tank 
to the solar collectors. Cooling mode is set with the parameter Tanks 
recooling (SP051) which determines the period during which cooling will 
be authorised.
This function is only activated if the temperature of the solar collectors is 
below the maximum cooling temperature determined by the parameter

increase during cooling, it will stop for a set period of two hours. The

12.7.4 Periods of absence or going on holiday
Important
Do not power off, disconnect, or switch off the indoor unit so that 
the heating pump anti-blocking function is able to run and protect 
the installation against freezing.
Your appliance will automatically regulate the heating based on the 
outdoor temperature. If you prefer, you can shut off the heating regardless 
of the outdoor temperature whilst continuing to use the domestic hot water 
and cooling functions.
If you are away from home for several weeks, you can reduce the room 
temperature and domestic hot water temperature in order to save energy. 
For this, activate the System holiday mode operating mode for all zones, 
including the domestic hot water, or the Holiday operating mode for each 
zone individually.
Activating holiday mode for all zones
If you are away from home for several weeks, activate the System holiday 
mode operating mode for all zones, including domestic hot water. The 
room setpoint temperature is lowered to 6 °C and the domestic hot water 
setpoint is set to the DHW eco setpoint parameter.
The outdoor unit will maintain the flow water temperature at 25 °C to 
protect the system when the outdoor air temperature is below 5 °C.
1. From the home screen, press the button.
2. Select System holiday mode.
3. Enter the start and end dates and times for the absence period.
4. Select Confirm to confirm the setting.

12.9 Starting and stopping the heat pump
12.9.1 Starting the heat pump
1. Switch on the outdoor unit and the indoor unit.
The heat pump will begin an automatic vent cycle (which lasts 
approx. three minutes), run each time the power is switched on.
2. Switch on the backup boiler, if fitted.
12.9.2 Shutting down the heat pump
The heat pump must be shut down in certain situations, for example 
during any intervention on the equipment. In other situations, such as an 
extended absence period, we recommend that the System holiday mode 
operating mode is used in order to benefit from the heat pump antiblocking function and to protect the installation from frost.
To shut down the heat pump:
1. Shut off the heating or the cooling.
2. Switch off the power to the outdoor unit.
3. Switch off the power to the indoor unit.
4. Switch off the backup boiler, if fitted.

13.1 Prolonged power outage in winter
A prolonged power outage at outdoor temperatures below zero may 
damage your heating installation. Action may be required, depending on 
the configuration of your installation:
Installation with glycol: no action required.
Installation equipped with anti-freeze valves: drain the outdoor part of 
the heating installation during a prolonged power outage (10 hours or 
more) at outdoor temperatures below zero.
Important
If in doubt about the draining and filling procedure, contact your 
installer.

13.2 Draining an installation equipped with anti-freeze valves
A power outage of 10 hours or more at outdoor temperatures below zero 
may damage your heating installation. The outdoor section of the heating 
installation must be drained using the manual drain valves.
1. Switch off the outdoor unit at the electrical panel.
2. Locate the anti-freeze valves (a) installed outdoors, near the outdoor 
unit. 
3. Check whether water runs out of the anti-freeze valves.
Water runs out Action to be taken
Yes No immediate risk of freezing. 
Regularly check the anti-freeze 
valves until the power is restored.
No Follow the procedure with steps 4 
to 7.
4. Locate the isolation valves (b) installed indoors, on the heating circuit.
5. Close the isolation valves to isolate the outdoor unit from the indoor 
section of the heating circuit.
6. Locate the drain valves (c) installed indoors, on the heating circuit 
between the isolation valves and the outdoor unit, at the lowest point 
in the heating circuit.
7. Open the drain valves and drain the outdoor section of the heating 
circuit.
The outdoor unit is protected from frost.
8. Contact the installer to perform recommissioning.

14.1 General
An annual inspection with a leak-tightness check of the heating installation 
in accordance with prevailing standards is obligatory.
Maintenance operations are important for the following reasons:
To guarantee optimum performance
To extend the life span of the equipment
To provide an installation which offers the user optimum comfort over 
time
Caution
Only qualified professionals are authorised to carry out 
maintenance work on the heat pump and the heating system.
Danger of electric shock
Before any work, switch off the power supply to the heat pump 
and the backup boiler or the heating element, if present.
Danger of electric shock
Check the discharge from the capacitors of the outdoor unit.
Caution
Do not drain the installation, except in cases of absolute 
necessity. E.g.: several months' absence with the risk of 
temperatures in the building falling below freezing.

15.1 Resolving operating errors
When your appliance malfunctions, the display turns red and may flash. A 
message is displayed with an error code on the home screen.
This error code is important for the correct and rapid diagnosis of the type 
of malfunction and for any technical assistance that may be needed.
If an error occurs:

installer.
3. Switch off the outdoor unit and the indoor unit.
4. Switch on the indoor unit then the outdoor unit to check that the cause 
of the error has been removed.

A blocking code signals an anomaly affecting the heating system.
Several possibilities:
The system automatically attempts to correct the error (for example in 
the event of a fault related to the flow rate).
The error is still present and the system functions in defect mode (for 
example, in the event of a fault affecting the outdoor unit, then the 
backup electric heater or the backup boiler is started up).
The system is shut down but automatically switches on again when the 
error disappears.

# Part 1: Quick reference

## 1.1 Two sets of error codes on a Baxi HP55 system

1. **Controller codes** (this manual, pp.124-134), shown on the ASHP Control
   user interface: `Axx.xx` warning, `Hxx.xx` blocking, `Exx.xx` lockout.
2. **Outdoor unit codes** (outdoor unit manual pp.57-60), e.g. E0, E8, H6,
   P0, L-, J-, LC- codes, shown on the outdoor Main Control PCB display.

Many controller codes say "This error is generated by the outdoor unit. To
view the specific error code for the outdoor unit, refer to the error
details." So for those, open the error in **Error history** (Installer >
Error history, select the error, press the dial) to read the outdoor unit
code, then use the outdoor unit manual's code list for that code.

| Type | Format | Display colour | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Warning | Axx.xx | No colour change | Not optimal; keeps running; may clear itself | p.125 |
| Blocking | Hxx.xx | Continuous red | Anomaly; auto-retry, runs in defect mode on backup, or stops and restarts when cleared | pp.125-133 |
| Lockout | Exx.xx | Flashing red | Major anomaly, shut down. Remove the cause, then acknowledge the error manually on the user interface | pp.133-134 |

General user procedure (p.124): note the code, remedy or call the installer,
switch off the outdoor unit and indoor unit, switch on the **indoor unit then
the outdoor unit**, and if the code returns call the installer. Wait 3 min
for the outdoor unit capacitors to discharge before switching back on
(H06.28, p.129).

## 1.2 Commissioning on the controller (pp.37-41)

1. Refit all panels on the indoor and outdoor units, switch on the outdoor
   unit breakers, power the indoor unit. The Welcome message shows (p.37).
2. Either use the **Baxi START** app over Bluetooth (needs the BLE Smart
   Antenna PCB or the GTW-35 service tool) (p.37), or on the controller:
   Country and language, Date and time, daylight saving, then **CN1 and CN2**,
   then Confirm (p.38).
3. The heat pump runs a vent cycle (about 3 min, every power-up, p.122).
   If it won't start after venting, read the flow temperature: it must be
   above **6 °C** for the outdoor unit to start in heating; below that the
   backup runs first (p.38).
4. Set the backup type HP029 (p.39), the circuit function CP020 (p.41-42)
   and the heating curve (p.42-43).
5. Check the flow rate AM056 against the minimum (p.40): HP55-4/6/8:
   **6.6 l/min**; HP55-11/13 (1ph and 3ph): **11.7 l/min**. For radiators,
   set it with the compulsory pressure-actuated bypass valve; for UFH check
   the manifold valves open.
6. Final checks (pp.40-41): pumps and outdoor unit on, flow rate,
   temperature limiting device. Shut down, wait about 10 min, vent, check
   pressure (1.5-2 bar, p.37), clean filters, restart, explain to the user,
   hand over manuals.

**CN1 / CN2 for Assure HP55 (Tab.24, pp.38-39). CN2 is always 2.**

| Outdoor unit | CN1 | CN2 |
|---|---|---|
| Assure HP55-4-1-PHMB | 13 | 2 |
| Assure HP55-6-1-PHMB | 14 | 2 |
| Assure HP55-8-1-PHMB | 15 | 2 |
| Assure HP55-11-1-PHMB | 16 | 2 |
| Assure HP55-13-1-PHMB | 17 | 2 |
| Assure HP55-11-3-PHMB | 18 | 2 |
| Assure HP55-13-3-PHMB | 19 | 2 |

Values are also on the indoor unit data plate. Wrong or missing CN1/CN2 gives
H02.02 / H02.03 (p.127). After a PCB change, reset CN1/CN2 (p.55).

## 1.3 Key parameters (defaults from the parameter list, pp.56-70)

| Parameter | Code | Default / range | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installer code | – | 0012 (auto-exit after 30 min idle) | p.41 |
| CH function on / DHW function on | AP016 / AP017 | On / On | p.56 |
| Max CH flow setpoint | AP063 | 75 °C (20-75) | p.56 |
| Low pressure warning | AP058 | 0.8 bar (0-2) | p.56 |
| Deaeration program | AP101 | Always deair at power up | p.56 |
| Min CH pump speed | PP018 | 40 % (40-100) | p.56 |
| Backup type | HP029 | 1 Electrical Stage (No Backup / 1 / 2 stages / Boiler) | p.57 |
| Bivalent temperature | HP000 | 5 °C (-10 to 20) | p.57 |
| Delay start backup CH | HP030 | 0 min = automatic on outdoor temp | p.57 |
| Min outdoor T HP (compressor stops below) | HP051 | -20 °C (-25 to 5) | p.58 |
| Buffer tank / hysteresis | HP086 / HP087 | No / 3 °C | p.56 |
| Zone function | CP020 | Direct, Mixing Circuit (UFH on Zone1), Fan Convector, etc. | p.42 |
| Heating curve gradient | CP230 (Zone3 CP231) | UFH 0.4-0.7, radiators about 1.5 | p.43 |
| Max zone flow setpoint | CP000 (Zone3 CP001) | 75 °C (7-75) | p.43 |
| Thermostat contact logic | CP640 / CP690 | Closed / No | p.47 |
| Blocking input BL1 | AP001 | Full / Partial / User reset / PV / Smart Grid | pp.48, 53-54, 59 |
| Silent mode | HP058, HP094, HP095 | Level 1 or 2, start/end times | p.50 |
| Anti-legionella | DP004, DP160, DP410, DP430, DP440 | Off by default; 60-70 °C | pp.50-51 |
| Screed drying | ZP000-ZP090 (Zone3 odd numbers) | 3 stages; enable ZP090 | pp.45-47 |
| Frost min outdoor temp | AP080 | 3 °C | p.67 |

Useful signals (Installer > Signals, pp.67-69): flow rate **AM056** (l/min),
system flow temp AM016, HP flow/return HM001/HM002, compressor HM008,
backup HM012, BL1/BL2 contact HM004/HM005, defrost HM009, **IDU-ODU comm
quality HM024** (%), outdoor temp AM027, season mode AM091, 3-way valve AM037.

# Panasonic wired remote controller: navigation reference

Built 2026-10-23 from the two Panasonic manuals on file. This is the lookup
the assistant uses to give installers button-by-button steps on the wired
remote controller (the panel on the unit or wall, not a phone app).

- **Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32** (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5). Source:
  *Panasonic Service Manual, Mini Monobloc R32 J-series* (cite as "J-series
  SM, p.N"). The text came from the PDF's text layer, and most button icons
  inside sentences were lost ("Press  for 5 sec."). The original PDF arrived
  on 2026-10-24 (`manuals/panasonic/originals/Panasonic-J-series-Mini-Monobloc-R32-Service-Manual.pdf`),
  and the hidden-menu key combinations and error-history clearing (A4) were
  read from its page images.
- **Part B: K-series split Hydromodule + Tank** (WH-ADC0309K3E5/K3E5AN/K6E5/
  K6E5AN, outdoor WH-UDZ03/05/07/09KE5). Source: *Panasonic Installation
  Manual, Hydromodule + Tank K-series* (cite as "K-series IM, p.N"). Button
  steps here were read from the original PDF page images (pp.21-34), so the
  icons are known.

**Keep the parts separate.** The two manuals show the same button layout, but
menu lists, item numbers and hidden-menu key combinations are documented
separately. Never use a Part B key combination or menu item for a J-series
unit, or the reverse. If something is only in one part, say it is not
covered for the other model.

---

## Button names used in answers

Both manuals label the controller buttons A to G (J-series SM p.74, K-series
IM p.21). Use these names in every answer:

| Answer name | Manual label | Symbol on the button | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Menu]** | B: Menu | ☰ (three lines) | Open/close the main menu |
| **[▲] [▼] [◄] [►]** | C: Triangle (Move) | arrow keys | Select or change an item |
| **[OK]** | G: OK | ↵ (return arrow) | Confirm |
| **[Back]** | E: Back | ↩ (curved arrow) | Back to previous item |
| **[Quick Menu]** | F: Quick Menu | ⠿ (grid of dots) | Open/close the quick menu |
| **[Operate]** | D: Operate | ⏻ (power symbol, with LED) | Start/stop operation |

Layout on the panel (K-series IM p.21): top row Back, ▲, Menu; middle row ◄,
OK, ►; bottom row Quick Menu, ▼, Operate. Every list screen shows "Select"
(arrows) and "[↵] Confirm" in its footer.

---

# Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32

## A1. First power-up (J-series SM p.22, p.75)

1. Initialising screen shows for about 10 s, then the normal screen.
2. Press any button: the Language screen opens. [▲]/[▼] to choose, [OK].
3. Clock format 24h or am/pm: [▲]/[▼], [OK].
4. Date & time: arrows to set year/month/day/hour/min, [OK].
5. Back at the start screen. Press [Menu], select Installer setup.

If this initial setting is not done, the controller will not go into the
menus (p.75).

## A2. Main menu tree (J-series SM pp.23-36, p.75)

[Menu] opens Main Menu. Items 1-4 are user menus, 5-7 installer.
J-series SM p.23: "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting."

- **Function setup**: Weekly timer, Holiday timer, Quiet timer, Room heater,
  Tank heater, Sterilization (p.23)
- **System check**: Energy monitor, System information, Error history,
  Compressor, Heater (p.24)
- **Personal setup**: Touch sound, LCD contrast, Backlight, Backlight
  intensity, Clock format, Date & Time, Language, Unlock password (4 digits,
  default 0000) (pp.24-25)
- **Service contact**: Contact 1 / Contact 2 (p.25)
- **Installer setup** (pp.26-36, flow chart pp.76-77)
  - **System setup**, in this order: Optional PCB connectivity, Zone &
    Sensor, Heater capacity, Anti freezing, Tank connection, DHW capacity,
    Buffer tank connection*, Tank heater (only if Tank connection = Yes),
    Base pan heater, Alternative outdoor sensor, Bivalent connection,
    External SW, Solar connection*, External error signal*, Demand
    control*, SG ready*, External compressor SW*, Circulation liquid,
    Heat-Cool SW*, Force heater, Force defrost, Defrost signal, Pump
    flowrate. (*Only shown when Optional PCB connectivity = Yes; optional
    PCB is CZ-NS4P, p.66.)
  - **Operation setup**: Heat, Cool (cooling unlocked only), Auto (cooling
    unlocked only), Tank (only if Tank connection = Yes)
  - **Service setup**: Pump maximum speed, Pump down, Dry concrete, Service
    contact

## A3. Step-by-step recipes (J-series)

General path into any installer item:
0. **Turn the heat pump OFF first:** press [Operate] (⏻) so the operation LED goes out. Installer setup can't be opened while the unit is running (J-series SM p.23: "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting"; confirmed on site by Donal, HMG Field Notes 2026-10-23). Remind the installer to switch it back on with [Operate] when finished.
1. [Menu] (top-right button)
2. [▼] to **Installer setup**, [OK]
3. [▲]/[▼] to System setup / Operation setup / Service setup, [OK]
4. [▲]/[▼] to the item, [OK]
5. [▲]/[▼] (or [◄]/[►] on multi-field screens) to change, [OK] to store
6. [Back] to step out, [Menu] to close

**Check it changed:** open the item again and read the value back. Where a
setting has a visible effect, it is listed below.

| Task | Path after "Installer setup" | Options / default | Check it changed | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| External room thermostat (or internal, room thermistor, water temp) | System setup → Zone & Sensor | Without optional PCB: Water temperature / Room thermostat (Internal or External) / Room thermistor. Default "Room and Water temp." | Main screen sensor-type icon changes (p.21 lists Water temperature, Compensation curve, Direct, Room thermostat External, Room thermostat Internal, Room thermistor icons) | pp.26, 78; wiring examples pp.64-65 |
| 2-zone / pool | System setup → Optional PCB connectivity = Yes, then Zone & Sensor → 1 or 2 zone | Pool only on zone 2 | Zone 1 / Zone 2 appear in Operation setup | pp.26, 78 |
| Backup heater capacity | System setup → Heater capacity | 3 / 6 / 9 kW depending on model | Re-open item | pp.26, 78 |
| Anti freezing | System setup → Anti freezing | Yes (default) / No | Re-open item | pp.26, 78 |
| Tank connected | System setup → Tank connection | No (default) / Yes | Tank temp appears on main screen; Operation setup shows Tank | pp.26, 78 |
| Tank heater internal/external | System setup → Tank heater | Internal (default) / External + ON time 0:20 | Re-open item. Also set Function setup → Tank heater ON to use it (p.79) | pp.27, 79 |
| Bivalent (boiler) | System setup → Bivalent connection → Yes → Auto or SG ready → pattern | Alternative / Parallel / Advanced parallel; ON temp -5 °C default | Boiler icon on main screen (p.80) | pp.27-29, 80 |
| Glycol | System setup → Circulation liquid | Water (default) / Glycol | Re-open item | pp.30, 82 |
| Pump control mode | System setup → Pump flowrate | ΔT (default) / Max. duty | Re-open item | pp.31, 82 |
| Heating curve or fixed flow temp | Operation setup → Heat → Water temp. for heating ON → Compensation curve or Direct | Curve default: -5 °C → 55 °C, 15 °C → 35 °C. Direct default 35 °C. Range 20-60 °C. HMG recommends: steel rads -3 °C → 45 °C, 15 °C → 35 °C; UFH -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C; HMG max flow 45 °C rads, 35 °C UFH (HMG weather compensation guidance) | Main screen temp-setting icon (curve vs direct), re-open item | pp.31-32, 83 |
| Heating OFF outdoor temp | Operation setup → Heat → Outdoor temp. for heating OFF | 24 °C, range 5-35 °C | Re-open item | pp.32, 83 |
| ΔT for heating | Operation setup → Heat → ΔT for heating ON | 5 °C, range 1-15 °C (not available if Pump flowrate = Max. duty) | Re-open item | pp.32, 83 |
| Backup heater rules | Operation setup → Heat → Heater ON/OFF | Outdoor temp for heater ON 0 °C; delay 30 min; ON at -4 °C, OFF at -2 °C of target | Re-open item | pp.32-33, 83 |
| Tank times, re-heat, sterilisation | Operation setup → Tank → Floor operation time / Tank heat up time / Tank re-heat temp / Sterilization | 8:00 / 1:00 / -8 °C / 65 °C 10 min | Re-open item | pp.34-35, 84 |
| Pump maximum speed, read flow rate, air purge | Service setup → Pump maximum speed | Screen shows Flow rate (0.1-99.9 L/min), Max. Duty (range 0x40-0xFF, 0xCE example), Operation (OFF / ON / Air Purge). [▲]/[▼] sets Max. Duty, [►] moves to Operation, [▲]/[▼] picks OFF/ON/Air Purge, [◄] goes back. [Operate] turns the pump off on either screen | Flow rate reading on the same screen; also System check → System information → Pump flowrate | pp.35, 84, 151-152 |
| Pump down | Service setup → [OK] → [▼] to Pump down → [OK] → ON → [OK]. [Back] cancels | Screen shows "Pump down operation in progress!"; press [Operate] to stop, screen returns to "[⏻] Start" | Message on screen | pp.36, 84, 150 |
| Screed drying | Service setup → Dry concrete → Edit → [OK]: set number of stages (1-99, [▲]/[▼], [OK]), then each stage's water temp (25-55 °C, 1 °C steps, [OK] per stage; [Back] returns to the previous stage). After the last stage it returns to the ON/Edit screen. Select ON → [OK] to start | Status screen shows Stage n/N, water set temp and actual temp; stage moves on each day. [Operate] stops it | Re-open item | pp.36, 84, 155-156 |
| Installer phone number | Service setup → Service contact → Contact 1/2 | Name and number | Personal menu → Service contact | pp.36, 84 |

User-menu recipes (no Installer setup needed):

| Task | Steps | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Error history | [Menu] → [▲]/[▼] to System check → [OK] → Error history → [OK]. Shows the last 4 errors, most recent at top | pp.24, 163 |
| Live readings (inlet, outlet, zones, tank, buffer, solar, pool, compressor frequency, pump flowrate) | [Menu] → System check → System information → [OK] | p.24 |
| Energy / COP | [Menu] → System check → Energy monitor | p.24 |
| Quick menu items | [Quick Menu] → [▲]/[▼] to select → [OK] to turn on/off. Items: Force DHW, Powerful, Quiet, Force Heater, Weekly Timer, Force Defrost, Error Reset, R/C Lock | p.22 |
| Clear a displayed error | [Quick Menu] → Error Reset. On the error screen itself, select Close / Reset and confirm. If the fault is still there, it returns | pp.22, 162 |
| Weekly timer / holiday / quiet timer | [Menu] → Function setup → item | p.23 |
| Language, clock, contrast | [Menu] → Personal setup → item | pp.24-25 |

## A4. Hidden menus (J-series): key combinations (read from PDF page images, 2026-10-24)

| Menu | Hold | Contents | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Maintenance menu** | **[Back] + [OK] + [►] for 5 s** | Actuator check (manual ON/OFF of each part; no protection, so never run the pump without water), Test mode (test run, not normally used), Sensor setup (offset -2 to +2 °C, only if a sensor is deviating; it affects temperature control), Reset password | pp.85, 158 |
| **Custom menu** | **[Menu] + [▼] + [◄] for 10 s** | Cool mode (with/without cooling, default without), Back-up heater use/not use (disables frost-protection heater, may cause H75), Reset energy monitor, Reset operation history (p.85 lists 4 items, p.159 shows only the first 3) | pp.85, 159 |
| **Forgotten password** | **[Back] + [OK] + [►] for 5 s** (only shown when locked) | Password unlock screen appears, press Confirm, password resets to 0000. Set it again | pp.85, 158 |
| **Unlock Cool mode** | **[Menu] + [▼] + [◄] for 5 s**, operation must be OFF | Opens the Custom menu on Cool mode. [OK], [▲]/[▼] to Enable or Disable, [OK]. [Back] to exit | p.153 |
| **EEPROM factory reset** | **[▲] + [▼] + [◄] + [►] together for 5 s**, only while the screen shows "Initializing" at power-up | Initialisation stops, "EEPROM setup" runs, then initialisation restarts and the clock blinks. Wipes settings back to factory defaults | p.154 |

Note: the Cool mode unlock hold is 5 s on p.153 but the Custom menu hold is
10 s on pp.85/159. Same buttons. If 5 s does not open it, hold for 10 s.

**Clear error history permanently (p.163):** [Menu] → System check → [OK] →
[▼] to Error history → [OK] (shows last 4 errors). Press [OK] ("Clear
history"), "Do you want to clear error history?" appears with No selected.
[◄] to Yes, [OK]. The list shows "--". [Back] to leave without clearing.

**Clear a displayed error (p.162):** on the error pop-up, [◄]/[►] to Close
or Reset, then [OK].

These match the K-series combinations, but they are quoted here from the
J-series manual itself, so they can be given for J-series units.

## A5. Gaps (J-series)

- Pump-down (p.150), pump-speed (pp.151-152), dry-concrete (pp.155-156),
  cool-unlock (p.153) and error-history (p.163) procedures were read from the

# HMG Primary Pipe Sizing Guidance (Panasonic J-series and K-series)

Cite as **"HMG sizing guidance"** (method: HMG Pro Academy Training Handbook Level 1, pp.36-38; flow rates: HMG Panasonic nominal flow rate table).

Applies to the **primary pipework from the heat pump (outdoor unit) to the 3-way valve and the bypass / buffer**, i.e. the run that carries the heat pump's full flow.

**Panasonic only.** Do not use these figures for the Baxi Assure HP55 (or any other make). For the Baxi, use the flow rates and hydraulic data in the Baxi HP55 IM.

Originals: `sizing/originals/HMG-Pro-Academy-Pipe-Sizing-pp36-38.pdf`, `sizing/originals/panasonic-nominal-flowrates.png` (supplied by Donal Reilly, 24/10/2026).

---

## 1. The method (HMG Pro Academy handbook, pp.36-38)

Two equations combined.

**Mass flow rate (p.36)**
- Q = P ÷ (SHC × ΔT), Q in l/s
- For pipe sizing Q must be in m³/s: Q = P ÷ (1000 × SHC × ΔT)
- P = heat pump output (kW), SHC = specific heat capacity of water (4.2), ΔT = flow minus return temperature (°C)

**Pipe size (p.37)**
- A = Q ÷ V (A in m², Q in m³/s, V = velocity in m/s)
- A = πr², so d = 2 × √(Q ÷ (π × V)) in metres
- × 1000 for mm: **d = 2000 × √(Q ÷ (π × V))**

**Combined (p.38)**
- **d = 2000 × √(P ÷ (1000 × SHC × ΔT × π × V))**, d = minimum **internal** diameter in mm

**Worked example (p.38):** 7 kW heat pump, ΔT 5°C, velocity 0.9 m/s
- d = 2000 × √(7 ÷ (1000 × 4.2 × 5 × 3.14 × 0.9))
- d = 2000 × √(7 ÷ 59,346) = 2000 × √0.000118 = 2000 × 0.0109
- **d = 21.73 mm** internal

**Design velocity:** HMG recommended maximum is **1 m/s**, to avoid too much velocity (Donal Reilly, 24/10/2026). The handbook's worked example uses 0.9 m/s. Size at 1 m/s unless the installer chooses lower, and never pick a tube that runs over 1 m/s.

If you start from a flow rate in l/min instead of kW: Q (m³/s) = l/min ÷ 60,000, then d = 2000 × √(Q ÷ (π × V)).

## 2. Panasonic nominal flow rates (HMG table, J-series and K-series)

| Heat pump capacity | Nominal flow rate |
|---|---|
| 5 kW | 14.3 l/min |
| 7 kW | 20 l/min |
| 9 kW | 25.8 l/min |
| 12 kW | 34.4 l/min |
| 16 kW | 45.9 l/min |

These are the kW ÷ (4.18 × 5°C ΔT) flows, so the table assumes a 5°C ΔT.

## 3. Cross-check against the Panasonic manuals

| Size | HMG table | J-series SM (heating) | K-series IM rated flow (cool / heat) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 kW | not listed | not in J range | 9.2 / 9.2 l/min (WH-UDZ03KE5) | K-series only. Not in HMG table. |
| 5 kW | 14.3 | 14.3 l/min, WH-MDC05J3E5 (p.12) | 14.3 / 14.3 (WH-UDZ05KE5) | Matches |
| 7 kW | 20 | 20.1 l/min, WH-MDC07J3E5 (p.15) | 19.2 / 20.1 (WH-UDZ07KE5) | Manuals say 20.1 heating (rounded to 20 in HMG table). K-series cooling is lower, 19.2. |
| 9 kW | 25.8 | 25.8 l/min, WH-MDC09J3E5 (p.18) | 23.5 / 25.8 (WH-UDZ09KE5) | Matches for heating. K-series cooling is lower, 23.5. |
| 12 kW | 34.4 | not covered (J-series SM covers 05/07/09 only) | not covered (K-series IM covers 03-09 only) | From HMG table only |
| 16 kW | 45.9 | not covered | not covered | From HMG table only |

K-series rated flows: K-series IM p.8. J-series flows are "based on nominal capacity, LWT 35°C and ΔT 5°C" (J-series SM p.12).

Other manual points that matter for sizing:
- **Minimum flow:** both manuals say confirm the maximum water flow with the main pump running is **not less than 15 l/min** (J-series SM p.63, K-series IM p.12). Low flow at low water temperature can trigger H75 during defrost. On a 5 kW (14.3 l/min nominal) size the pipe so the circuit can actually pass 15 l/min. At 1 m/s that is 17.8 mm internal (18.8 mm at 0.9 m/s), still 22 mm copper.
- **Connections:** J-series monobloc water inlet/outlet are Rp 1¼" (J-series SM p.53, spec tables p.12). K-series tank unit space heating inlet/outlet are R1¼" (K-series IM p.5). The connection size is not the pipe size: size the pipe with the method above.
- **Insulation:** J-series SM p.53 says insulate the water circuit piping with 20 mm or more of insulation (condensation in cooling, heat loss, and freezing of outdoor pipework).
- **Glycol:** J-series SM recommends propylene glycol 40% where antifreeze is used. The HMG method uses SHC 4.2 (plain water). Glycol has a lower SHC, so it needs more flow for the same kW. Glycol correction is not covered by these sources.

## 4. Worked results (ΔT 5°C, SHC 4.2, max velocity 1 m/s)

Minimum internal diameter from the HMG equation at 1 m/s, then the smallest copper tube and the smallest MLCP pipe whose bore is at least that (so velocity stays at or under 1 m/s). The 0.9 m/s column is the handbook example velocity, for comparison.

| Heat pump | Flow (l/min) | Min bore @ 1 m/s | Min bore @ 0.9 m/s | Copper (velocity) | MLCP 2 mm wall (velocity) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 kW (K-series) | 9.2 (rated) | 14.0 mm (size for 15 l/min: 17.8 mm) | 14.7 mm | 22 mm (0.48 m/s) | 26 mm (0.40 m/s) |
| 5 kW | 14.3 | 17.4 mm | 18.4 mm | 22 mm (0.74 m/s) | 26 mm (0.63 m/s) |
| 7 kW | 20 | 20.6 mm | 21.7 mm | 28 mm (0.62 m/s; 22 mm would be 1.04) | 26 mm works (0.88 m/s), **32 mm preferred** (0.54 m/s) |
| 9 kW | 25.8 | 23.4 mm | 24.6 mm | 28 mm (0.80 m/s) | 32 mm (0.70 m/s; 26 mm would be 1.13) |
| 12 kW | 34.4 | 27.0 mm | 28.4 mm | 35 mm (0.69 m/s; 28 mm would be 1.06) | 32 mm (0.93 m/s) |
| 16 kW | 45.9 | 31.1 mm | 32.8 mm | 35 mm (0.92 m/s) | 40 mm (0.75 m/s; 32 mm would be 1.24) |

**7 kW on MLCP (HMG, Donal Reilly 24/10/2026):** 26 mm works, but 32 mm is preferred to allow for bends and elbows. 26 mm runs at 0.88 m/s with only 0.3 mm of bore to spare at the handbook's 0.9 m/s.

Velocities use the method's flow (kW ÷ (4.2 × ΔT)); the table's nominal flows give the same answers.

Key point for installers: **22 mm copper is too small for a 7 kW** (bore about 20.2 mm, the 7 kW needs 20.6 mm at 1 m/s and 21.7 mm at 0.9 m/s). It would run at about 1.04 m/s, over the 1 m/s max.

### Copper bore figures used (HMG to confirm)

The HMG handbook gives the required internal diameter but no copper tube bore table. To pick a tube size the assistant uses EN 1057 R250 standard wall copper:

| Copper OD | Wall | Bore |
|---|---|---|
| 15 mm | 0.7 mm | 13.6 mm |
| 22 mm | 0.9 mm | 20.2 mm |
| 28 mm | 0.9 mm | 26.2 mm |
| 35 mm | 1.2 mm | 32.6 mm |
| 42 mm | 1.2 mm | 39.6 mm |

**Pending Donal's confirmation** (24/10/2026): whether these are the bores HMG wants used. (Max velocity confirmed by Donal: 1 m/s.) Other pipe materials (e.g. PEX) have different bores: use the pipe maker's internal diameter.

### MLCP (multilayer composite pipe)

HMG uses MLCP with a **2 mm wall** (Donal Reilly, 24/10/2026), so bore = OD − 4 mm:

| MLCP OD | Wall | Bore |
|---|---|---|
| 16 mm | 2 mm | 12 mm |
| 20 mm | 2 mm | 16 mm |
| 26 mm | 2 mm | 22 mm |
| 32 mm | 2 mm | 28 mm |
| 40 mm | 2 mm | 36 mm |
| 50 mm | 2 mm | 46 mm |

The OD range is the usual MLCP size range; some makers use 25 mm instead of 26 mm, or a thicker wall on larger sizes. If the pipe on site differs, use its actual bore.

## 5. How the assistant should answer a sizing question

1. Confirm the unit (Panasonic J-series monobloc or K-series split) and its kW. If it's a Baxi, say this HMG guidance is for Panasonic only and use the Baxi manual.
2. Take the nominal flow from the HMG table (or the manual's rated flow for the 3 kW K-series).
3. Use ΔT 5°C and the 1 m/s maximum velocity unless the installer gives other values; say which values you used. Never recommend a tube running over 1 m/s.
4. Give the minimum internal diameter, then the copper size and the MLCP (2 mm wall) size with the velocity in each, unless the installer names one material. Show the sum briefly.
5. Remind them of the 15 l/min minimum flow check at commissioning and 20 mm+ insulation on outdoor runs.
6. Cite: "Source: HMG sizing guidance (Pro Academy handbook pp.36-38; HMG Panasonic flow rate table)" plus the manual page for any manual figure.
7. Out of scope (say so): pressure drop / pump head for long runs, glycol correction, emitter-side sizing, Baxi or other makes.

# HMG Outdoor Unit Clearances

Cite as **"HMG clearance guidance"** (Donal Reilly, 24/10/2026), plus the manual page where the manual is quoted.

Minimum clear space from the outdoor unit to a wall, fence or other obstacle. Left and right are taken **looking at the front of the unit (the fan / air outlet side)**. Keep each unit separate: never quote one unit's figures for another.

---

## HMG figures (Donal Reilly, 24/10/2026)

| Unit | Rear | Right-hand side | Left-hand side | Front |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Panasonic J-series Mini Monobloc R32 (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5) | 300 mm | 300 mm | 100 mm | 1000 mm |
| Baxi Assure HP55 R290 monobloc (all models) | 300 mm | 300 mm | 100 mm | 1000 mm |
| Panasonic K-series split outdoor unit (WH-UDZ03/05/07/09KE5) | 100 mm | 300 mm | 100 mm | 1000 mm |

---

## Cross-check against the manuals

### Panasonic J-series monobloc: the service manual gives no clearance figures

Checked against the original J-series Service Manual PDF on 2026-10-24. p.52 (12.1.1 Select the Best Location) says "keep minimum distance of spaces as illustrated above from wall, ceiling, or other obstacles", but the only drawing on the page is a sketch of the unit with three leader lines and **no dimensions or labels**. No other page in the 246-page manual gives clearance or service-space figures (searched the full text; p.38 is unit dimensions only: 1284 W × 865 H × 400 D mm). So the HMG figures (rear 300, right 300, left 100, front 1000) **cannot be confirmed or contradicted from this manual**: no differences to flag, but no backing either. The figures would be in the J-series *installation* manual, which is not on file.

Page image: `clearances/originals/panasonic-j-series-sm-p52-location-drawing.png`.

Other p.52 siting points from the manual:
- Outdoors only, on a flat solid surface; avoid sites below -20°C ambient.
- Good air circulation, easy drainage, accessible for maintenance, away from heat sources and flammable gas leaks.
- Don't obstruct the discharge air (no short-circuiting) and avoid the suction side facing straight into the wind.
- An awning must not block heat radiation from the condenser.
- Exposed or windy sites (rooftops, between buildings): fix with an overturn prevention wire (fitting K-KYZP15C).
- Fix to a concrete floor with M12 anchor bolts at 4 points, pull-out strength above 15000 N. Concrete compressive strength above 18 MPa.
- With the drain elbow: stand taller than 50 mm, cover the other 8 holes (ø20 mm) with rubber caps. Don't use the elbow and caps where it stays below 0°C for 2-3 days (drain water freezes and the fan won't turn).

### Baxi Assure HP55: manual asks for more on the sides, and more at the front on 11 and 13 kW

Baxi HP55 IM p.32 (6.2.2 Minimum distances from the walls, Fig.21 and 22):

| Baxi letter | Where | HP55-4/6/8 | HP55-11/13 | HMG figure | Match? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E | Rear (back to wall) | ≥ 300 | ≥ 300 | 300 | Yes |
| B | Front (air outlet) | ≥ 1000 | **≥ 1500** | 1000 | Yes on 4/6/8. **No on 11/13: manual says 1500.** |
| G | Right-hand side | ≥ 500 | ≥ 500 | 300 | **No: manual says 500** |
| F / H | Left-hand side | ≥ 500 | ≥ 500 | 100 | **No: manual says 500** |
| A | Base above ground | ≥ 100 | ≥ 100 | none given | Manual only. Allow for snow (footnote, p.32). |
| C | Top of unit to an obstacle above | ≥ 500 | ≥ 500 | none given | Manual only |
| D | Overhang of an obstacle above, past the unit | ≤ 500 | ≤ 500 | none given | Manual only |

Between units (p.33, Fig.23): back to back ≥ 600 mm (V); front to front ≥ 2500 mm on 4/6/8, ≥ 3000 mm on 11/13 (W); side by side ≥ 500 mm (Y).
Cold climates (p.34): back of the unit towards the wall; at least 100 mm between the unit and the mean snow cover.

**HMG decision (Donal Reilly, 24/10/2026): installers follow the HMG figures.** Give the Baxi manual figures as a note only.

**R290 protective perimeter (Baxi HP55 IM pp.30-31).** Separate from the clearances above, and applies as well:
- Free-standing on the ground or a flat roof (Fig.18): 1000 mm all round the unit.
- In front of a wall (Fig.19): 300 mm behind (to the wall), 1000 mm in front. At the sides it is 500 mm at the top of the unit, widening to 1000 mm at ground level. Its height H is at least the height of the unit above the ground.
- In a corner (Fig.20): 300 mm behind, 500 mm to the side wall, 1000 mm on the open side at ground level, and it extends up to 1800 mm in front. See the drawing on p.31.
- Inside the perimeter: no openings into the building (doors, windows, skylights, air vents, lightwells, cellar access, sewer hatches), no permanent ignition sources (lights, switches, sockets), no temporary ignition sources (lawnmowers, barbecues, cigarettes), and it must not adjoin alleys, parking spaces, neighbouring plots or public areas (p.30). It applies to wall-mounted units too and extends to the ground. Open condensate gullies inside it are not a safety risk (p.36).
- R290 is highly flammable (A3) and heavier than air, so it collects at ground level.

Page images: `clearances/originals/baxi-hp55-protective-perimeter-p31.png`, `clearances/originals/baxi-hp55-wall-clearances-p32.png`.

### Panasonic K-series outdoor unit: the service manual agrees with HMG

Checked against the K-series Service Manual (Order No PCZ2508021CE, 2025) on 2026-10-26. p.94 (12.3.2.1 Installation Diagram) shows the same clearances for both drawings (WH-UDZ03KE5, and WH-UDZ05/07/09KE5): **100 mm rear, 100 mm left-hand side, 300 mm right-hand side, 1000 mm front**, all "or more". That is exactly the HMG figure, so there are no differences to flag.

Page image: `clearances/originals/panasonic-k-series-sm-p94-installation-diagram.png`.

Other siting points from the manual (cite "K-series SM"):
- Avoid more than 2 blocked directions; for multiple outdoor units, consult the dealer (p.94).
- Fix the unit firmly and level on concrete or a rigid frame with ø10 mm bolts and nuts. On a roof, allow for strong wind (p.94).
- With the drain elbow: a stand taller than 50 mm and rubber caps on the other ø20 mm holes (7 on the 3 kW, 3 on the 5-9 kW). Where it stays below 0 °C for 2 or 3 days running, don't use the drain elbow and caps: the drain water freezes and the fan won't turn (p.94).
- Avoid sites that drop below -20 °C (3 kW) or -25 °C (5, 7 and 9 kW). Don't block the discharge air or let it short-circuit. An awning must not block the heat radiation from the coil (p.93).
- A base pan heater (CZ-NE2P, optional) is strongly recommended in cold areas (p.93).
- 5, 7 and 9 kW: fit the discharge grille (supplied) before powering on (p.95).

---

## Not covered

- J-series clearance figures (not in the service manual; installation manual not on file).
- Clearances above the unit and between multiple units for the Panasonic units.
- Building regulations, planning or noise distance rules.

# HMG Weather Compensation Curve Settings

Cite as **"HMG weather compensation guidance"** (Donal Reilly, 25/10/2026), plus the manual page for the controller steps.

HMG recommended heating curve (weather compensation) starting points. Two points on the curve: the flow temperature the heat pump aims for at -3 °C outdoors (design cold day) and at 15 °C outdoors (mild day). Set the curve at commissioning, then fine-tune for the house.

---

## HMG recommended curves (Donal Reilly, 25/10/2026)

| Emitters | Flow at -3 °C outdoor | Flow at 15 °C outdoor |
|---|---|---|
| Steel radiators | 45 °C | 35 °C |
| Underfloor heating | 35 °C | 25 °C |

**Maximum flow temperature (HMG rule, any heat pump): 45 °C on steel radiators, 35 °C on underfloor heating.** Never set the flow higher than this, whatever the outdoor temperature (Donal Reilly, 25/10/2026).

Same HMG figures for all three units (Panasonic J-series, Panasonic K-series, Baxi HP55). Only the way you enter them on the controller differs.

Both curves have the same slope: 10 °C of flow over 18 °C of outdoor change, about 0.56 °C of flow per 1 °C outdoor.

---

## Panasonic J-series and K-series: enter the four points directly

The Panasonic compensation curve is set as four temperature points (2 outdoor, 2 water), so the HMG figures go in exactly as they are.

Path: Installer setup → Operation setup → Heat → Water temp. for heating ON → Compensation curve.

- Outdoor (X axis) low point: **-3 °C**; flow (Y axis) at that point: **45 °C rads / 35 °C UFH**.
- Outdoor (X axis) high point: **15 °C**; flow (Y axis) at that point: **35 °C rads / 25 °C UFH**.
- Maximum flow: the -3 °C flow point is the top of the HMG curve, so it must be no higher than **45 °C rads / 35 °C UFH**. The Panasonic manuals on file have no separate maximum flow setting, so the curve point is how you hold it. Note the factory curve goes to 55 °C at -5 °C, which is over the HMG maximum for both, so always change it.
- Factory default: -5 °C → 55 °C, 15 °C → 35 °C. Range: outdoor -20 to 15 °C, water 20 to 60 °C (WH-MDC). The HMG figures are inside the range.
- 2-zone system: the four points must be entered for Zone 1 and Zone 2 separately (e.g. rads on one zone, UFH on the other).
- With a room thermostat or room thermistor, the curve can still be used; the unit shifts it with the thermostat on/off (heats up very slowly → shift up; very fast → shift down).
- Installer setup is locked while the unit runs: switch off with [Operate] first, then [Menu]; switch back on with [Operate] at the end.

Manual pages: J-series SM pp.31-32 and p.83 (12.4.4 Operation Setup, item 24); K-series IM p.31 (3-4 Operation Setup, item 26). Room thermostat / thermistor shift: J-series SM p.65, K-series IM p.14.

---

## Baxi Assure HP55 (ASHP Control): gradient + base temperature

The Baxi controller doesn't take two points. It uses a gradient (CP230) and a curve base temperature (CP210), and works out the flow setpoint from the room setpoint (Baxi ASHP Control IM p.74):

CM070 (flow setpoint) = (CM190 room setpoint − CM210 outdoor temp) × CP230 + CP210 (when CP210 is above 15 °C).

Worked out from that formula for the HMG curves, with a **20 °C room setpoint**:

| Emitters | CP230 gradient | CP210 base (comfort) | CP000 max flow | Gives at -3 °C | Gives at 15 °C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Steel radiators | 0.6 | 32 °C | 45 °C | 45 °C (capped) | 35 °C |
| Underfloor heating | 0.6 | 22 °C | 35 °C | 35 °C (capped) | 25 °C |

(The exact HMG slope is 0.56; 0.6 is the nearest 0.1 step, which would give about 45.8 / 35.8 °C at -3 °C. CP000 caps it at the HMG maximum.)

- **Maximum flow (HMG rule): set CP000 (Zone3 CP001) to 45 °C for radiators or 35 °C for underfloor.** Factory setting is 75 °C on Zone1 (50 °C on Zone3), well over the HMG maximum, so always change it. The heat pump-wide Max CH flow setpoint AP063 (Heat Pump › General, default 75 °C, IM p.56) can also be set to 45 °C (or 35 °C on an underfloor-only system).

- Path: [Menu] › Installer (code 0012) › Installation setup › Zone1 (or Zone3) › Heat curve. Zone1: CP230 gradient, CP210 comfort base, CP220 reduced base, CP000 max flow. Zone3 uses CP231, CP211, CP221, CP001.
- CP220 is the base used in reduced (eco) periods. Set it the same as CP210 if you don't want a lower curve in reduced periods.
- The curve only works with an outdoor sensor and control strategy CP780 (Zone1 > General) on Automatic, Outdoor temp based, or Outdoor & room based (not Room temp based). Factory setting is Automatic (IM p.63, p.73).
- The room setpoint moves the curve: each 1 °C above 20 °C raises the flow by about 0.6 °C (the gradient). If the room setpoint isn't 20 °C, re-work the base: CP210 = flow at 15 °C − (room setpoint − 15) × 0.6.
- Check it changed: Installer › Signals › Zone1 › Zone Tflow Setpoint CM070 should be close to the curve for today's outdoor temperature (CM210).
- Baxi's own guide (IM p.43) says UFH gradient 0.4-0.7 and radiators about 1.5. The HMG radiator gradient (0.6) is much flatter than Baxi's 1.5 because HMG designs radiators for a 45 °C maximum flow. Use the HMG figures.
- Fine-tune by 0.1 every 24 hours, mid-season then mid-winter (IM p.42).

Manual pages: Baxi ASHP Control IM pp.42-43 (8.4.1 Setting the heating curve), p.61 (Tab.47 Heat curve parameters, ranges: gradient 0-4, base 15-90 °C, max flow 7-75 °C Zone1), p.63 (CP780), pp.73-75 (9.2.5 Operation of the heating curve, formula and examples).

---

## Commissioning notes

- These are starting points. If the house is short of heat on cold days, raise the -3 °C flow point (Panasonic) or the gradient (Baxi). If it's short on mild days, raise the 15 °C point (Panasonic) or the base (Baxi). Change a little at a time and give it a day.
- Never set the flow above the HMG maximum (45 °C rads, 35 °C UFH), or the emitter or screed maker's maximum if that is lower.

# Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32 (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5)

## 1. Before you switch on

- **Pipework and wiring finished.** All water pipework and electrical cable connections are properly done before filling or test run (J-series SM p.63).
- **Pipe duct sealed and dry.** The duct carrying the flow and return pipes between the outdoor and indoor unit is sealed and has no water in it. A wet duct makes the unit run constantly and trip on F12 (HMG Field Notes – F12 high pressure trips on site).
- **Cylinder sensor in place.** If there is a DHW cylinder: the cylinder sensor is fully in the sensor pocket at the correct position, so it reads the real cylinder temperature. A misplaced sensor causes F12 trips (HMG Field Notes – F12 high pressure trips on site).
- **Fill and purge the water circuit.** Remove the cover (2 screws). Turn the air purge valve plug anticlockwise one full turn. Set the pressure relief valve lever DOWN. Fill at more than 1 bar through the water inlet until water flows freely from the pressure relief valve drain hose (J-series SM p.62).
- **Water only, no glycol.** HMG recommends water only in the circuit (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Set Circulation liquid to Water in stage 3, and keep Anti freezing on Yes. Note: the manual itself recommends 40% propylene glycol (J-series SM p.63).
- **Expansion vessel big enough.** Built-in vessel is 6 L at 1 bar pre-charge, good for up to 150 L of system water without antifreeze. Over 150 L, or with glycol, add a vessel. If the highest point is more than 7 m above the unit, set the pre-charge to (height in m × 10 + 30) kPa (J-series SM p.62).
- **Water pressure.** With all power off, fill to **1 to 1.5 bar** on the unit's water pressure gauge (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Never lower than 0.05 MPa (0.5 bar) (J-series SM p.62).
- **Pressure relief valve tested.** Turn the lever horizontal and listen for the clack of water draining, then push the lever back down. If water keeps draining, switch off and escalate (J-series SM p.62).

## 2. First power-up

- **Power on, pump running, no leaks.** Switch on the supply and check the water pump runs and there are no leaks at the pipe connections. Refit the cover (J-series SM p.62).
- **RCCB tested.** With power on, press TEST on the RCCB: the lever drops to 0. Touch nothing else inside. Set the lever back ON (J-series SM p.63).
- **Language, clock and date set.** About 10 s after power-up, press any button: choose the language, clock format (24h) and date and time, [OK] after each. The controller won't open the menus until this is done (J-series SM p.22, p.75).

## 3. System setup (unit OFF)

- **Get into Installer setup.** Press [Operate] ⏻ so the operation light goes out, then [Menu] (top right) › Installer setup › System setup. Installer setup is locked while the unit runs (J-series SM p.23; HMG Field Notes – Can't get into Installer setup).
- **Optional PCB connectivity.** Yes only if the optional PCB (CZ-NS4P) is fitted, e.g. for 2 zones, solar or SG ready. Otherwise leave No (J-series SM p.26, p.66).
- **Zone & Sensor.** HMG: **Room thermostat, External**, with the weather compensation curve (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Options are Water temperature, Room thermostat (Internal or External) or Room thermistor; 1 or 2 zones with the optional PCB (J-series SM p.26, p.78).
- **Heater capacity.** HMG: **3 kW** backup heater on the 5, 7 and 9 kW models (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Options 3, 6 or 9 kW depending on model (J-series SM p.26, p.78).
- **Anti freezing.** HMG: **Yes** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (J-series SM p.26).
- **Tank connection and tank heater.** If a DHW cylinder is fitted: Tank connection = Yes, then Tank heater = Internal or External (factory Internal, ON time 0:20). To use the tank heater also set Function setup › Tank heater ON (J-series SM pp.26-27, p.79).
- **Bivalent connection.** Only if a boiler is connected: Yes › Auto or SG ready › pattern (Alternative, Parallel, Advanced parallel). Otherwise leave No (J-series SM pp.27-29, p.80).
- **Circulation liquid.** Water or Glycol, to match what's in the system (J-series SM p.30, p.82).
- **Pump flowrate.** HMG: **ΔT** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Other option Max. duty (J-series SM p.31, p.82).

## 4. Operation setup › Heat

- **Heating curve (HMG).** Operation setup › Heat › Water temp. for heating ON › Compensation curve. HMG: steel radiators -3 °C outdoor → 45 °C flow, 15 °C → 35 °C. Underfloor -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C. The factory curve (-5 °C → 55 °C) is over the HMG maximum, so always change it. On 2 zones set Zone 1 and Zone 2 (HMG weather compensation guidance; J-series SM pp.31-32, p.83).
- **Maximum flow (HMG).** Never above 45 °C on radiators or 35 °C on underfloor. On the Panasonic the -3 °C curve point is the maximum: there is no separate maximum flow setting in the manual (HMG weather compensation guidance).
- **Outdoor temp. for heating OFF.** HMG: **24 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Range 5-35 °C (J-series SM p.32, p.83).
- **ΔT for heating ON.** HMG: **5 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Range 1-15 °C (J-series SM p.32, p.83).
- **Heater ON/OFF.** HMG: outdoor temp for heater ON **-3 °C** (factory 0 °C) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Leave the rest at factory: delay 30 min, heater ON at 4 °C below target water temperature, OFF at 2 °C below (J-series SM pp.32-33, p.83).

## 5. Operation setup › Tank (cylinder only)

- **Tank timings.** HMG: Tank re-heat temp **-8 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Leave Floor operation time (8:00) and Tank heat up time (1:00) at factory (J-series SM pp.34-35, p.84).
- **Sterilization (legionella).** HMG: **65 °C for 10 min** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Operation setup › Tank › Sterilization. Set the day and time to suit the customer in Function setup › Sterilization (J-series SM pp.23, 34-35, p.84).

## 6. Service setup

- **Air purge.** Service setup › Pump maximum speed › [►] to Operation › [▲]/[▼] to Air Purge › [OK]. Run it until the flow reading is steady. [Operate] stops the pump (J-series SM p.35, pp.151-152).
- **Flow rate checked.** Read Flow rate on the same screen. Must be at least 15 l/min with the main pump running; low flow can cause H75 during defrost (J-series SM p.63). Nominal flow: 5 kW 14.3, 7 kW 20, 9 kW 25.8 l/min (HMG sizing guidance; J-series SM p.12). HMG: leave pump Max. Duty at the factory setting, adjusting only if the site needs it (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).
- **Service contact.** Service setup › Service contact › Contact 1: HMG: **Heat Merchants Technical Support** (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (J-series SM p.36). No phone number needed.
- **Screed drying.** Only on a new screed floor: Service setup › Dry concrete › Edit, set stages and temperatures (25-55 °C), then ON. Follow the screed maker's schedule (J-series SM p.36, pp.155-156).

## 7. Test run

- **Start the unit.** Press [Operate] ⏻ to switch back on and run heating (J-series SM p.63).
- **Pressure while running.** Gauge reads between 0.05 and 0.3 MPa (0.5 to 3 bar) (J-series SM p.63).
- **No leaks.** Check every water connection for leaks during the test run (J-series SM p.53).
- **Flow rate, all zones open.** With the heating running and every zone valve open, read the flow: [Menu] › System check › System information › Pump flowrate. It should be at least 15 l/min and close to the unit's nominal flow from stage 6 (J-series SM p.24, p.63; HMG commissioning check, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).
- **Flow rate, all zones closed (bypass).** Close every zone so all the flow goes through the bypass valve. Read the flow again in the same way, and adjust the bypass valve until it reaches the unit's nominal flow rate from stage 6 (HMG: nominal flow across the bypass, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).
- **No errors.** [Menu] › System check › Error history: nothing new. Clear old install errors: [OK], [◄] to Yes, [OK] (J-series SM p.24, p.163).
- **Water filter cleaned.** After the test run, clean the water filter and refit it (J-series SM p.63).

## 8. Handover

- **Explain it to the customer.** Show the customer how to use the controller and how to look after the unit (J-series SM p.4).
- **Unit left running.** Unit ON at the controller, covers refitted, and Error history clear.
